reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is managing incomplete data within autonomous systems. The primitives form a cascading hierarchy: blocked sources are first isolated to prevent systemic contamination, then fallback mechanisms activate to maintain continuity, readiness metrics quantify the health of the system, and finally, the UI contracts serve as the final interface layer ensuring that users interact safely with potentially uncertain data. This structure mirrors information theory's rate-distortion tradeoff, where we balance the cost of full data acquisition against the distortion introduced by approximations. Inference failures occur when any link in this chain breaks, leading to either overconfident decisions or outright system halts. To model opposing agents, we assume rational actors who exploit gaps in the isolation protocols; thus, the primitives also function as a defensive architecture. Anti-collinearity is enforced through independent verification layers, while leakage vetoes ensure that downstream products do not inadvertently combine incompatible data streams.
